Package dev.px.core.setting

Class Setting<T>

java.lang.Object
dev.px.core.setting.Setting<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the value type
All Implemented Interfaces:
Named
Direct Known Subclasses:
BindSetting, BooleanSetting, ColorSetting, EnumSetting, GroupSetting, MultiEnumSetting, NumberSetting, RangeSetting, StringSetting
public abstract class Setting<T> extends Object implements Named
A single named, typed, persistable value owned by a SettingHolder.

Replaces the old Setting<T> with its five overlapping constructors and instanceof type-sniffing. Each concrete subclass knows its own type, so GUI code dispatches on the class rather than guessing from the value, and serialisation is the setting's own job instead of a giant switch in a file utility.

Instances are created through the factories on Settings (or the shorthands inherited from SettingHolder) and are discovered automatically — declaring the field is the whole registration step.

      public void set(T newValue)

    • setSilently

      public void setSilently(T newValue)
      Assigns a value without notifying anyone.

      Used when loading a config: firing a change event per setting during a profile load would have modules reacting to half-applied state.
